messages:
Alex: :rotating_light: Observing error spike on prompt-routing v2 canary, outbound latency up ~4x for small requests. Customer-facing latencies degraded for a subset of sessions. Paging oncall.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created (INC-7421) — paging SRE oncall. Escalation: 5m.
Maria: I'm seeing a cluster of 503s from the new endpoint /v2/prompt-route. TTLs look normal. Metrics: increased retry rate -> queue growth on canary nodes.
Jay: Can somebody confirm which FF rolled the canary traffic? I see a rollout to 18% earlier today: flag=ff.prompt_routing_experimental -> target: canary pool.
Sophie: Confirmed. That flag was flipped at 08:12 deploy window. I routed 18% to canary for QA smoke.
Kunal: Oncall taking this. I'm switching traffic off the experimental route now — plan: kill switch the FF and re-evaluate. @ops-bot can you run a quick toggle?
ops-bot: Received command. Ready to execute. Please provide flag key.
Kunal: ff.prompt_routing_experimental
ops-bot: Executing toggle -> setting flag ff.prompt_routing_experimental = OFF for all environments.
ops-bot: Done. Confirmed: rollout aborted, target overridden to default routing.
Alex: Observability — dropping latency within 60s? Watching request queue and KV cache pressure.
Maria: 30s in — tail latencies dropping, error-rate down from 12% to 1.8% on affected route. Looks like immediate improvement.
Jay: Nice. Any customer impact to call out? Any customers on dedicated routes hit hard?
Sophie: Replaying a few support tickets — two customers reported elevated latency > 2s for chat sessions. No long-term data loss, just added retries.
Kunal: Paging update to stakeholders: FF killed, canary evacuated. Next steps: abort rollout entirely, pin stable model, and run a rollback for the control-plane change that enabled new KV sharding.
Alex: Do we need to do a full rollback or can we let the flag remain off and monitor? What's the risk of leaving the flag off?
Maria: The flag being off returns system to previous behavior. We should let it stabilize for 30m, but I recommend a targeted rollback of the control-plane sharding if we see any regression in 15m.
Kunal: Agreed. I'll keep the oncall seat; handoff only when things quiet. Notifying sales and support: small customer-facing latency spike, mitigated by feature flag abort.
incident-bot: Incident INC-7421 status -> mitigation: FF aborted. Assigned to Kunal for investigation.
Jay: Recording commands for postmortem:
```
# kill switch via ops-bot
ops-bot toggle ff.prompt_routing_experimental off
# verify
kubectl logs -n inference svc/prompt-router-canary | tail -n 200
```
Kunal: I'm capturing logs and traces. Pulling canary pod logs and cache stats now, will attach links.
Sophie: I'll draft the initial customer impact note for support: brief summary + mitigation steps + ETA for RCA.
Maria: One more note — we saw a surge in small payloads (<=64 tokens) causing an unexpected batching interaction with continuous batching heuristics. That seems correlated with the sharded KV change. Put that in the triage.
Alex: Good catch. If KV sharding caused cross-pod cache misses, we'd see increased latency for short requests. That matches the symptom set.
Kunal: For now: status = mitigation in place, flag killed, canary evacuated, monitoring sustained improvement. I'll keep channel updated; if latency creeps back up I'll escalate.
Sophie: :white_check_mark: I'll update support and put a note in the incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident INC-7421 — last update recorded at 2112346012.
Kunal: Planning a handoff to Maria in 30m if stable. Otherwise I'll remain on call.
Maria: Ack. I'll take it if things look green at the 30m mark.
Alex: Thanks team — solid quick action. We'll follow up with an RCA and a postmortem that covers rollout gating and FF kill-switch playbooks. :memo:
